scope: General shareable design decision synthesis; cross-index existing patterns rather than claim novel patterns. Candidate state-transition sources require full verification.

patterns.name: Color selection and semantic roles
patterns.definition: Choose by task, brand, context, neutral surfaces, accent, semantic states, tonal scale and contrast. Primitive → semantic → component/state tokens.
patterns.guardrail: Neutral-first for dense workspaces; expressive direction only if useful. 60/30/10 is optional, not a standard. Color psychology varies by context; never use color alone.
patterns.tests: Test all real foreground/background pairs, light/dark/forced colors, focus, alpha composition and gamut; inspect #103 contrast failures.
patterns.classification: Research synthesis; not exhaustive or independently tested

patterns.name: Data visualization color selection
patterns.definition: Categorical for unordered groups, sequential for magnitude, diverging around a meaningful midpoint.
patterns.guardrail: Do not conflate status and identity, imply magnitude in categories, or rely solely on hue.
patterns.tests: Test legend, labels, adjacent marks, missing data, color vision simulation and accessible data alternative.
patterns.classification: Research synthesis; not exhaustive or independently tested

patterns.name: Motion and animation decision framework
patterns.definition: Start with purpose: feedback, spatial continuity, reveal, progress, direct manipulation or emphasis. Choose fade/scale/slide/layout/shared element only when useful. Tween for predictable time; spring for spatial/direct manipulation with velocity.
patterns.guardrail: Frequent actions should be quiet and fast; no decorative delay or motion-dependent feedback. Productive vs expressive is guidance; 0/50/100/150/250/400/600ms illustrative only, not universal.
patterns.tests: Test entry/exit asymmetry, interruption, reversal, rapid input, reduced motion, transform/opacity where appropriate and frame cost.
patterns.classification: Research synthesis; not exhaustive or independently tested

patterns.name: Attention and visual hierarchy
patterns.definition: Use scale, contrast, typography, alignment, proximity, common region, whitespace, position and limited accents to establish order.
patterns.guardrail: Avoid competing highlights and obligatory F/Z layout; distinguish observed reading behavior from design rule. Preserve meaningful content.
patterns.tests: Compare alternatives with realistic tasks, comprehension, visual search and keyboard order.
patterns.classification: Research synthesis; not exhaustive or independently tested

patterns.name: Keyboard focus and selection management
patterns.definition: Keyboard focus is not hover, selection or active route. Visible focus, meaningful order, return focus on dismissal; move focus logically when element removed. Avoid stealing focus on async updates.
patterns.guardrail: WCAG 2.2 2.4.3 A, 2.4.7 and 2.4.11 AA, 2.4.13 AAA; 1.4.11 when applicable; follow widget APG. Focus trapping only appropriate modal context.
patterns.tests: Test keyboard, screen reader, focus visibility/adjacency, sticky header obstruction, modal open/close and preservation across refresh.
patterns.classification: Research synthesis; not exhaustive or independently tested

patterns.name: Screen architecture and composition
patterns.definition: Map tasks, objects, flows and information hierarchy before visual design. Choose single-column for focused reading/form, list-detail for browsing, supporting pane for related context, tabbed workspace/split for multiple objects, dashboard for analytics, canvas for spatial tasks.
patterns.guardrail: Do not force 3 panes, cards or borders everywhere. Use modular spacing, meaningful groups, readable type, consistent iconography, progressive disclosure and task-driven density.
patterns.tests: Test multiple layouts via sketch/wireframe; verify mobile/tablet/desktop, container reflow, zoom, input modalities, preservation of state, scroll and focus.
patterns.classification: Research synthesis; not exhaustive or independently tested

patterns.name: Interaction and component state modeling
patterns.definition: Define default, hover, focus-visible, pressed, selected, checked/indeterminate, expanded, open, dragging, readonly, invalid and disabled where relevant. Separate variant, event and semantic state; document simultaneous states and precedence.
patterns.guardrail: Do not infer behavior from screenshots; don't force irrelevant states. Focus and selection remain separate; touch/no-hover alternatives.
patterns.tests: Matrix of real component states, keyboard/touch/assistive tech, accessibility semantics, styling precedence, before/after evidence.
patterns.classification: Research synthesis; not exhaustive or independently tested

patterns.name: Data and asynchronous state modeling
patterns.definition: Distinguish initial loading, refresh, empty, partial, stale, pending, optimistic, success, error, timeout, retry, offline, conflict, permission denied, cancel, undo and unsaved. Track operation state separately from data and visual animation.
patterns.guardrail: Never report success or progress without confirmation; preserve data/context on refresh; avoid race and duplicate submission.
patterns.tests: Test out-of-order response, double click, cancel, retry, timeout, rollback, permission, offline, stale data, status messages and focus.
patterns.classification: Research synthesis; not exhaustive or independently tested

patterns.name: Logical state transition contract
patterns.definition: Specify from, event, guard, to, effects, invariants, timers, concurrency and cancellation. State machine/statechart useful for complex workflows; no required library for simple state.
patterns.guardrail: Separate logical change from visual duration; valid states and unreachable transitions must be defined. Model example: selected → submitting → correct/incorrect/error; retry and cancel explicit.
patterns.tests: Test allowed/disallowed transitions, guards, rapid repeated actions, abort, racing requests, rollback, idempotence and invariant checks; don't pass expected state into runtime.
patterns.classification: Research synthesis; not exhaustive or independently tested

patterns.name: Visual transition and motion choreography
patterns.definition: Choose visual transition by source/destination, spatial relationship, intent and input. Document enter/exit, crossfade, push, reveal, scale, expand/collapse, reorder, shared element, gesture/spring and route transitions.
patterns.guardrail: CSS transitions, CSS animation, WAAPI and View Transition API are techniques, not semantic state. Verify support and fallback. Don't defer focus, result or interaction until animation completion.
patterns.tests: Capture before/during/after, durations and easing only if measured or source verified; test cancel/reverse, rapid input, reduced motion and keyboard.
patterns.classification: Research synthesis; not exhaustive or independently tested

patterns.name: Iterative design and validation workflow
patterns.definition: User needs → tasks → IA → flows → sketches/wireframes → visual direction → states/motion → tokens → prototype → testing → iteration. Typography, iconography, shape, elevation, copy, density and perceived performance are cross-cutting.
patterns.guardrail: Iterative, not mandatory linear process; design systems and aesthetics do not prove usability.
patterns.tests: Evidence packet with alternatives, rationale, contraindications, accessibility, source/version, tests and unresolved gaps; #94 prevents synthetic benchmarks claiming real quality.
patterns.classification: Research synthesis; not exhaustive or independently tested
